en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Garlic 3.
The Training Rule on Striking with the Palm.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, two bhikkhunīs, oppressed by lack of lust, entered a small room and were slapping their palms together.
The bhikkhunīs, hearing that sound, ran up to them and said to those bhikkhunīs:
"Why, noble ladies, are you consorting with a man?"
“We do not, noble ladies, have illicit relations with men,” they reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can these bhikkhunīs clap their hands?”... [and so on].
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs are slapping their palms?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
“How indeed, bhikkhus, can bhikkhunīs clap their hands?
This, bhikkhus, is neither for the inspiration of those without confidence nor for the increase of confidence in those who have it...
And thus, bhikkhus, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:”
“Regarding ‘a slap on the palm, there is an offense of expiation’:
a ‘slap on the palm’ means that if she consents to physical contact and gives a blow to the vagina with even a lotus leaf, there is an offense of expiation.”
There is no offense:
in the case of illness,
or for one who is insane.
"By one who is a first offender.
The third training rule is concluded.
